title: Pattern matching — quick overview
rememberThis: is and switch expressions are the two main hosts for patterns. Declaration patterns also introduce a variable only when the match succeeds.
Switch expressions return a value and must be exhaustive — use the discard (_) for everything left, or throw.
Relational patterns compare to constants. Combine them with and, or, not — not with && inside the pattern.
with on a record copies and sets named properties. It does not mutate the original. Nested lists are still shared unless you replace them.
Auth branching belongs in a switch expression over a closed set of provider records — not scattered magic strings in controllers.
bullets: Expression-bodied members use => on methods, properties, and constructors — they are not lambda delegates.
List patterns with .. slice handle ragged comma-separated values (CSV) rows whose column count varies.
null is a constant pattern; is not null is the logical not of that constant and ignores overloaded ==.
Enums are not truly closed at run time — an enum variable can hold any int, so keep a discard arm.

rows.label: Switch statement vs expression
rows.value: Statement: labels, no fall-through (except empty cases). Expression: arms return a value, must be exhaustive.

rows.label: Property pattern
rows.value: { Scheme: "LTI", Version: "1.3" } matches those fields; nested patterns go inside braces.

rows.label: List pattern
rows.value: [_, "DEPOSIT", .., var amount] — positional match on array or list-like sequences.

rows.label: with expression
rows.value: var next = current with { ExpiresAt = utc }; shallow copy for records and record structs.
